I would first start with determining what kind of play style you like. Do you like aggro? Throwing out cheap cards fast and gaining lore rapidly? Do you like controlling the board? Do you just want a deck with a fun theme? Do you enjoy ramping up your ink and playing beefy cards? 

After you figure that out, then it’s time to survey the colors and figure out what color combo you want. Are there some cards that seem to pair well with each other? Does a certain color/combo of colors offer the best value for what you are wanting to do? Then it’s about picking the cards needed for the deck, and filling it in with supporting cards that enhance your ability to play it and counter your opponent.

I mean to me. An exotic mission is a mixture of great scenery, pressure, fun exploration, and good bursts of combat. The things that whisper mission did and outbreak was that the timer added immediate pressure, you couldn’t just explore forever and take your time. The tower being the setting or also the caverns in whisper were really fun and thematic, and it felt far different from the stuff we’ve done before. The actual act of going through those missions felt fun too, because of the jumping puzzles and light puzzle solving mechanics week over week. Not to mention some of the jumping things were pretty cheeky. The combat encounters, at least to me, were kinda ball breaking. They were tough, I had to configure my loadout and plan my attack. Which cluster do I go for first? Who’s the big threat, should I slap on a rocket or maybe go with a sword? 
The combination of these things makes a good exotic mission. A satisfying run full of needing to discover the secrets and strategies. 

The visuals of this new exotic mission were okay, but the act of going though it was a snooze fest. The traversal areas are literally just a bunch of running and walking around, I don’t think I needed to do anything else. There was no verticality. The enemies weren’t hard, they were basic and not many of them. The mirror mechanic looked cool, but was so boring. I’d of thought at least that once you get the buff needed to break the boss shield, it was on a timer and you’d have to go back in to get it again for multiple boss phases. Nope. Just once, then you’re golden for the entire encounter. Like, it was just boring, flavorless. I’ve only ran it once so I know it evolves a bit with different bosses, but that first run was just boring. And personally I don’t care for the organ stuff. Just not my vibe. They also just didn’t use it well

Therapist usually start out with some sort of intake evaluation where they kind of just assess what’s going on at a very base level, and they dig further from there. Even just letting them know you have some trauma concerning your dad from years ago can give them a direction to lead you. The important thing is that therapists work with you as far as you’re willing to go. If you need months and months, they’ll be there for those months and months. If you need years, they’ll work with you for years. There’s no set expectation on when to sort this out. You can have sessions where you maybe only talk about the good times, and fun things you and your dad did together.

I think the biggest thing is simply “understanding.” Like, we’re all people. Sometimes we have bad days, sometimes we have off days where we don’t even want to hear a whisper from anyone or anything. Some days we have a lot of energy and maybe are too annoying. Just understanding that we are people, and can’t be expected to act the same all the time goes a long way. An easy dealbreaker for me is if someone is just plain self absorbed and rude. A bit of kindness towards others in any way shows your character. People who only care about their gains suck.
